checks.finding: Core terms are concrete: SDD_PANELIST_TIMEOUT default 600s with exit-2 rejection rules (AC-003), and REQ-002's runtime table (requirements.md:57-60) specifies exact mechanisms per runtime (setsid plus a process-group SIGTERM for POSIX; Start-Process -PassThru plus WaitForExit plus Kill with the entire-tree flag for PowerShell) with matching sub-case assertions in acceptance-tests.md:64-76. The unspecified exact SIGTERM grace-period duration (requirements.md:59) is implementation latitude bounded by a generous 10s test margin (acceptance-tests.md:53), not a two-implementer-divergence risk, per the false-positive guard on implementation architecture.

No direct conflict found. The apparent asymmetry between POSIX's two-step escalation (SIGTERM then SIGKILL) and PowerShell's single unconditional tree-kill (requirements.md:59-60) is explicitly reasoned rather than contradictory: Process.Kill maps to TerminateProcess, which cannot be trapped, so a PowerShell (b) sub-case cannot fail (acceptance-tests.md:70) -- the remediation narrative (requirements.md:62) documents that a prior draft asserted a false equivalence here and was corrected. REQ-003's exit-1-for-timeout and AC-003's exit-2-for-bad-config are distinct failure classes (vendor non-response vs caller misconfiguration) with no overlap.

The round-1 finding is genuinely closed, not merely restated. requirements.md:59 now requires the POSIX child to start in its own process group (setsid) and be signalled via the group, explicitly not to the single PID, and AC-004's liveness-assertion column requires 'no orphan of any child the stub spawned remains' for POSIX, not only PowerShell. acceptance-tests.md:64-76 mirrors this: the TEST-004 sub-case table marks orphan-checking as required for both runtimes in row (a), and the attempt-2 remediation paragraph (acceptance-tests.md:74-76) states the stub spawns its own child and the POSIX assertion fails against a single-PID signal and passes only with the process-group signalling. A literal implementation that stores and signals a single pid (the round-1 gap) would leave that spawned grandchild alive and fail TEST-004(a) on POSIX, so the loophole is closed by an executable assertion, not by prose alone. Edge Cases 1-7 each map to a specific AC/TEST pair.

The SIGTERM-termination assumption (requirements.md:176) is not left open -- Edge Case 7 mandates a test whose stub traps SIGTERM specifically to exercise the SIGKILL escalation path, closing the assumption with a test rather than deferring it. The install.sh:758-781 citation's missing INV- provenance (requirements.md:177) is explicitly flagged as a recorded gap, and the requirement it supports is stated to rest independently on Edge Case 1's first-hand command -v result, so the gap does not block design. The three investigation Open Questions for #133/#134 are each resolved by name in the requirements text (AC-002 for rate-limiting, AC-013/REQ-004 for the MCP-checklist question, AC-014 for the residual-risk cross-linking question).

REQ-005/AC-010 requires docs/THREAT-MODEL.md to name the hook-trust governance-bypass flag explicitly and state what an operator who uses it forfeits (requirements.md:131-133), and this is testable via TEST-010 (acceptance-tests.md:16,94-98), which asserts both the literal identifier and an accompanying trust/mitigation statement. This is the one approval/governance-adjacent boundary this feature's scope touches, and it is testable as required rather than left as an unverifiable narrative claim.

The specification supplies enough concrete detail that a design reviewer need not invent product behavior: REQ-002's runtime table names exact mechanisms and signal targets per runtime (requirements.md:57-60), REQ-001's five-mode failure taxonomy with per-mode exit code / verdict-file / propagation requirements is fully enumerated (requirements.md:25,31-39), and REQ-004/REQ-005's five undocumented trust surfaces are named with a two-part verification (identifier plus trust/mitigation statement, requirements.md:123-133). No requirement defers a product decision to the design stage.

No domain/ directory exists at the project root (confirmed via Glob for domain and domain/*, both returning no matches), so the check's applicability precondition is not met. Recorded as skipped per the check's own skip condition.
